maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: But the whole objection so far has been that I am proposing to discuss the pension group of items one after another instead of skipping about from one branch of the department to another. I have stated that for the greater convenience of the committee we would, if the committee agree, begin with the functions of the pension commission generally. Perhaps this would not be quite the proper item on which to discuss the proposed amendments, but the next which I suggest that we should take up, the vote of forty odd millions of expenditure in the way of pensions, would be an appropriate item on which my hon. friend could make all the suggestions he pleases with regard to amendments to the Pension Act.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
Under the rules of this
house and of the British parliament administration items bring into review the whole administration of matters relating to returned soldiers. In the British house the other day this same question was up, and it was not dealt with in a technical way. Representing
Supply-Pensions

a city which sent, more soldiers to the great war than any other city in Canada, I am surprised that twenty-one years after the war returned soldiers are still walking the streets looking for employment while employment commissions and committees usurp the powers of this house. What has been done since the last session? There are rules and regulations that ex-soldiers be given preference-

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
I regret to interrupt, but
surely the hon. member is out of order.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
Positions on the bench,
positions in the senate and positions all through the civil service-

speakerposition: Deputy Chair of Committees of the Whole
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Order.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
-are being given to
civilians, while soldiers are walking the streets.

speakerposition: Deputy Chair of Committees of the Whole
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
Order. The
vote before the committee is No. 215, details of which will be found at page 153, dealing with the Canadian pension commission.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: No; it deals with administration expenses-

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Of the commission.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
-which involves the
whole problem of administration.

speakerposition: Deputy Chair of Committees of the Whole
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
The hon.
member should confine himself to the matter before the committee.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
I understood that years
ago. I was in the house before the hon. member. I am here to-day as a representative of the people, and you are not going to pass five cents of this item until I have my say. I know the rules of the house, and if necessary I shall appeal to the Speaker.

speakerposition: Deputy Chair of Committees of the Whole
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: That is the hon. member's privilege. But he, or any other hon. member of the committee, must confine his remarks to the vote before the committee. The minister has pointed out that in another vote, one for S40,900,000, general remarks may be made, but they cannot be made on this vote.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
With all due deference to you, sir, I think you are wrong. I submit that the vote for administration expenses involves the whole problem of administration and everything connected with it. Even if we wished to, we could not cut down the vote for 140,900,000. We cannot in any sense amend it, because it is statutory and fixed by law. We have no control over it. That

item for $40,900,000 is something which, under a statute of parliament, we are bound to vote. The amount has been determined by the pension commission.
But under the present vote we are dealing with administration expenses, and the vote involves the problem of administration, details of which are set out at page 153. There we have the whole problem, including the number of men employed, the reasons for their employment, and everything connected with the matter.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: I regret to take issue with my right hon. friend on the point, but I believe if he would read from page 27 of the estimates he would find, under item 213, provision for departmental administration.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: I have read it.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
Item No. 213 deals with departmental administration.	On that vote
perhaps the point would be well taken. Departmental administration would cover any matter which is now being discussed, and with respect to which I called the hon. member to order. It would cover unemployment, because such salaries are covered by departmental administration.	If the right
hon. gentleman will observe what is written in the book of estimates he will find that item No. 215 follows the item of salaries of commissioners, and that the administration expenses are those of the Canadian pension commission. The Canadian pension commission do not deal with unemployment, but deal purely with pensions.
I think on reflection the right hon. gentleman will come to the conclusion that in all probability under the present item any hon. member could discuss anything connected with pensions or with the Canadian pension commission, but it would not be competent for him to discuss any other matter which would come under some other branch of the department.
With respect to the contention of my right hon. friend that the $40,900,000 represents a statutory provision, may I say that that is so, but only to a certain extent. It is not statutory in the sense of a fixed vote being statutory. It cannot be, because the evidence is right here.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: I do not suggest it is, with respect to salaries.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
It is not statutory in the sense that the salary of a commissioner is statutory, where is it set down in the legislation that the commission chairman shall receive a salary of so much and that the members of the commission shall receive so much. That is statutory, in the real sense of

Supply-Pensions
the word. But to say that a vote of $40,900,000 is statutory, and that it has to be voted, is going a bit far.
Last year it was $41,500,000, and that was not statutory. On reflection I think my right hon. friend will come to the conclusion that there is a vast difference between a fixed sum to be paid out of the consolidated revenue fund, and so stated in the statutes, and an amount which may vary from year to year.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
I think I can make
perfectly clear the difficulty the minister has indicated. A statutory obligation may be of a twofold character. It may be indicated in terms as to what the amount of the statutory claim may be, such as judges' salaries, salaries of commissioners and matters of that kind. Then there is the second type-

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Which need not be voted.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: This amount, do you say?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: No, the first part, marked with the letter "S".

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Yes. But the amount of $40,900,000 is statutory, because it is a computation passed under the terms of a statute, which cannot be modified without repeal. That is the whole position. That is, under authority of a statute, $40,900,000 must be provided.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: It must be voted.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: No; it must be provided and voted under authority of the statute. Therefore it is a statutory obligation of the Dominion of Canada and, as such, cannot be lessened, unless the statute is amended or repealed.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Oh, yes; adjudication can change it.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
On the adjudication as made, this is a statutory obligation now fixed at $40,900,000, on a series of computations, which computations are made under the terms of the statute. They cannot be more or less, once the adjudication is made, unless under authority of the statute.
Suppose we were to pass a resolution reducing the item by a million dollars, hon. members will realize that at once we would have the position of having contravened a provision of the statute.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: No.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Yes, because adjudication is made under the statute, and the provision at once makes it a statutory obligation.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
The
numbers entitled to pension might vary, from year to year, under the statute.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: The minister answers my question when he adds the words, "under the statute."

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: I should say consequent upon the statute.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: There can be no variation in the item, except under the statute.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: The minister would have no alternative except to bring in legislation to change the system of adjudication.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: That is my view.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: But we have strayed away from the theoretical point as to whether or not it is statutory. Perhaps I would agree with my right hon. friend that in one sense it is but in another it is not. It is not statutory in the sense that it shall be passed without discussion by the committee.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Correct.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: The item of $40,900,000- which, by the way, is not before the committee-is an item which is always discussed and can properly be discussed by the committee, even though there might be some doubt as to the propriety-yes, I will say more than that-or as to the legality of someone moving to reduce it.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: That is the point I made. At page 151 we find the branch administration details.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: We are not on that yet.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: We are on item No. 215, which item deals with administration expenses, and follows the words "salaries of commissioners," which has reference to the administration by the commissioners.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Of the commission only.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Yes, I say that. It is not the administration of the department, but the administration of the pension commission as found at page 153 in the details. That opens up the whole question of the administration by the commission of the Pension Act.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Of pensions.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Not departmentally.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
May I be permitted a word of explanation of the new form of estimates, as it might apply to discussion. It
Supply-Pe nsions

was the intention, in preparing the new form, to have one item, and one only, in each department under which the general discussion of the administration of that department would be facilitated. The balance of the items deal with specific matters. That is the case in each department. However, in the case of this department there are two administrative items, one relating to the department generally. being No. 213, and the other one relating to the administration of the pension commission. The reason for these items is to give opportunity for the ordinary discussion of pensions administration apart entirely from the discussion of other aspects of departmental matters and thus to get rid of the somewhat confusing discussion which has occurred in the past in committee of supply when one member would ask a question relating to some particular matter and another member would follow with a question relating to something else miles away. The hope is to give better service to the members of the committee by way of information and by confining the discussion within reasonable limits. The present vote would permit a discussion of everything connected with the administration by the pension commissioners of the work entrusted to them, but I submit that it does not permit a discussion of other aspects of departmental work.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Mr. Chairman, may I be permitted to say a few words about this item of $534,330, being a decrease of $18,196 from last year? The details of this item are to be found at pages 151 and 153 of the estimates. I am surprised that there should be a necessity for such a large number of officials twenty years after the war. In the details I see listed a deputy minister, an assistant deputy minister, a draughtsman, stenographers and clerks. Is it not the duty of all these officials to see that the act is carried out? Is it not the duty of these officials to see that preference is given to returned soldiers? I am receiving letters all the time from all over Canada complaining about the administration of this act. Returned soldiers cannot get a job on the Canadian National Railways, and twenty years after the war there is still plenty of evidence that returned men are out of work. I think it would be better if we had a committee of ten or fifteen members to which these estimates could be referred so that there might be a businesslike discussion of this matter.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Would the minister give the particulars of the item of $6,500 for materials and supplies, as set out on page 153?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: That would cover stationery and other supplies needed by the office of the Canadian pension commission and its employees throughout the country.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: I was surprised to hear the minister give such a strict interpretation of the rules of procedure. I can remember that when he was sitting to the left of the Speaker he was not quite as strict in his observance of the rules.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
Owing to the looseness of
the rules he was probably able to carry on in a manner which was embarrassing to the minister and at the same time to some hon. gentlemen on the other side of the chamber. With the desire to endeavour to reform the procedure he suggested very humbly that perhaps better progress could be made and a better understanding of this whole pension problem arrived at by proceeding in an orderly and leisurely fashion. I have no objection to going back to the old rough and tumble scramble where everybody talks at once on every possible subject, but I think it would be more in order if the committee would deal only with pensions at this time.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: I realize it is far better that we should conduct our business in an orderly manner, but I notice that the minister has chosen an appropriate time to start this orderly way of doing business. However, I rose in my place to ask for a little information. I notice from the details on page 153 that the number of employees in the department has been reduced to some extent as compared with last year. Could the minister state if that reduction has been made because of there being less work in the department, because we have reached the peak so far as this work is concerned, or is it for other reasons?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
Does the hon. gentleman
refer to the decrease in the amount of the item?

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: No, in the number of employees.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
There is a decrease of nine, due largely to the fact, I believe, that a number of employees of the Canadian pension commission were absorbed into other branches of the department. As a result of an amendment in 1936 to the Pension Act the department received authority to take over employees from the pension commission. Prior to 1936 there were two so-called water-tight compartments, the departmental employees and the Canadian pension commission employees. It is now possible for the department to draw on the pool in the pension

Supply-Pensions
commission. My hon. friend is quite right in thinking that to some extent the work of the pension commission has decreased. He will notice on looking at the estimates that the amount involved in the payment of pensions is considerably less than it was last year.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: How many pension commissioners are there at the present time? I notice from the annual report of the department that the arrears of cases have been practically eliminated. It was our understanding that as soon as the arrears were caught up with the number of commissioners would be reduced, thereby decreasing the expense.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: When I came into the department there were twelve commissioners. One commissioner was added under the legislation of 1936, but four retired last year. At the present time there are nine commissioners, a decrease of three as compared with August, 1936.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Will the minister explain the item of $40,000 for professional and special services?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: That refers to the employment of outside professional men, mainly doctors, etc. I have not the list before me, but I believe there are probably ten or fifteen specialists in Toronto, with the same number in Montreal and a proportionate number in other cities, who may be called from time to time. This vote would be for fees to be paid to these men.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Would they all be medical men?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: All medical men.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: What would the special services cover?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: There might be the odd amount for legal fees if the pension commission decided to prosecute in cases of fraud, but I do not know of any during the past year.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Would the minister explain the item of $75,240 for temporary assistance?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
Under some kind of regulation of the moguls of the treasury board it is impossible to make more than a certain percentage of the employees of a department permanent. Only 80 per cent can be made permanent; the remainder are temporary employees, and the only nomenclature I can find for them is temporary-permanents or permanent-temporaries. Some of them have been in the department for five or six years or more; but there is a rule now, generally observed 51952-32
throughout the whole civil service, that only 80 per cent of the employees in any department shall be permanent.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Are these employees engaged by the civil service commission?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Yes, all of them.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: How many members of this staff are returned men?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Ex-service men comprise 92 per cent of the male staff of the whole department.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Is there any reason why it should not be 100 per cent?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: There are such employees as office boys, and I suppose there is an odd instance of a technical man who has managed to get in. Then there are a few men who are not ex-service men, who have been in the department since its inception. I think my hon. friend would be pretty well satisfied if every department could show 92 per cent of ex-service men.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: Why have the office boys' salaries been materially reduced?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: I do not know that they have been, but I shall be glad to look into the matter and have the office boys call on my hon. friend and see that he is satisfied.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
Would the minister
explain the item of $80,000 for transportation and travelling expenses?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext: That is for the travelling expenses of the quorum members, who, as my hon. friend knows, travel from one end of the country to the other and hold sittings; also for travelling expenses of pensioners and applicants. Reverting to the question of office boys, I find that there were two office boys, and now we have only one, so I shall be able to send only one to my hon. friend.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
Consequent upon the
amendments of 1936 in regard to the staff of medical officers, I see there is a reduction of only one. Has their status in any degree been altered, or were there any transfers frim the department to the commission? Are thti solely responsible to the commission and not in part to the minister?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
Generally speaking, the
medical men who were connected with the pension commission have remained there. There has been no very great change. One was transferred to the health branch of the department because we needed a new man.

maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
Has the minister studied and is he quite satisfied with the expense of

Supply-National Revenue

running this department in relation to the amount of money the returned men are actually receiving? What percentage of the amount the men actually receive in money does the cost of operating the department represent?

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: PRINCE EDWARD ISLAND NATIONAL PARK-STATEMENT OF MR. BENNETT ON MOTION OF PRIME MINISTER
speechtext:
We have had calculations and estimates of that made during the last twenty years, and generally the minister contents himself with saying that the cost of administration is about three per cent. My hon. friend would probably find that it is more if he went into it, because I know that when I was sitting opposite I satisfied myself that the cost of administration, if one took into consideration overhead and one thing and another, would probably go over three per cent. But that arbitrary figure, so to speak, has been fixed for the last fifteen or twenty years, and we all stick by it because we do not know of any other. I move, Mr. Chairman, that this item stand.
Item stands.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE

speechtext: Customs and excise divisions-general administration, $1,106,150.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: What is the explanation of the increase in this item?

speakeroldname: Hon. J. L. ILSLEY (Minister of National Revenue):
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext:
The net increase in this item is $96,490, accounted for in this way:	the
increase in permanent salaries amounts to $82,990, made up as follows: Restoration of five per cent deduction, $44,880; statutory increases, $24,765; thirty-five temporaries made permanent, $33,840; salaries of three employees transferred from undervaluation branch and one from investigation branch, $5,880; additional amount required due to reclassifications and promotions, $5,065; making a total of $114,430. From that must be deducted the following: sixteen positions abolished, $23,865; saving by the promotion of officers at less salaries than paid their predecessors, $7,575; making total reductions of $31,440. That makes a net increase of $82,990, which accounts for the greater part of the $96,490 increase. The remainder is made up as follows: There is an increase of $25,700 in printing and stationery; a decrease of $10,000 in temporary salaries, and a decrease of $2,200 in travelling expenses. If the hon. member will add the $25,700, and subtract the $10,000 and the $2,200, he will get the net increase of $96,490.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext:
Why should the general
administration costs of this department rise so much? It is true that the revenues collected are considerably more than last year,

but the collections are made largely on the same number of items, the only difference being that the items themselves are larger. For example, it should not cost the department any more to collect $5,000 of a man's income tax than if S2.000 were collected from him the year before. How does the minister explain such a big increase in the administration? In round figures, surely only the same amount of work has to be done.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext:
I have just explained it.
The greater part of it is due to the restoration of the five per cent deduction. That comes to $44,880, and the statutory increases amount to $24,765. Then certain officers who have been classified as temporary have been made permanent, and that moves them from other estimates into these particular estimates and accounts for the increase of $33,840. I do not know that I can give the hon. gentleman any better explanation than that; but he will see that when you have to add nearly $45,000 on account of the restoration of the five per cent cut, and nearly $25,000 because of statutory increases, that is quite a big part of the increase which is shown here.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext:
Is that the final five per
cent?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: Then are we safe in saying, or can we hope, that you do not anticipate the continuance of this great big increase of $96,000 every year in the running of the administration?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext:
I do not anticipate it, no.
One can never tell. The hon. gentleman has himself pointed out quite a notable fact, that the collections of the Department of National Revenue as a whole-I am not speaking now of the customs and excise divisions-have increased enormously in the past two years. I quote now from memory and in round figures:	In the twelve months just
before I took over the office in October, 1935, the net collections for the department of national revenue were about $305,000,000, and for the twelve months two years later they were about $435,000,000. There has been a very great increase in the amount collected, and it is accounted for not merely by larger sums being obtained from the same number of transactions, but by a very great increase in the number of transactions, making necessary some increase in staff. But the figures that I have given show that most of the increases here are made up, not at all

Supply-National Revenue
by an increase in staff, but by restoration of the five per cent deduction and by statutory increases. The increase in staff is shown in the details at the back of the book.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext:
Of course it is quite true
that improved conditions of trade and commerce in Canada and generally throughout the world have naturally caused bigger collections to be made. But while we are making bigger collections, the effort of the department, one would think, would be to endeavour to get the same revenues at the same cost if possible. However, I am pleased to hear that the minister, in view of this five per cent now being added, which is the final addition to the one hundred per cent salaries that have been drawn, does not anticipate in the future these continued additions to general administration costs.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext:
I shall take the last five
years, for example, and give, not the figures of revenues and expenditures but the percentage cost of collection. Starting at 1930, that is for the year 1930, the percentage cost of collection in customs and excise was 3-30 per cent; in 1931, 4-45; in 1932. 4-87; in 1933, 3-86; in 1934, 3-37; in 1935, 2-97; in 1936, 3-20; in 1937, 2-71; and for the first nine months of 1937-38, 2-45.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext:
Of course the more you
collect the less the percentage should be.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: Well, it is going down pretty rapidly.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: It is quite natural that it should.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: That was not due to the minister's efforts; that was due to better times.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: I notice on page 147 of the estimates that the cost of temporary assistance for the year 1938-39 is estimated at $415,395, while for 1937-38 it was $210,455. That seems a striking increase in that service. Would the minister give the committee some details or an explanation of the reasons for that increase?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: This does not come under the vote that we are discussing, because temporary assistance is not under general administration, but I have no objection to going into it now if the hon. gentleman would prefer that I do so. One of the reasons for some increase in temporary assistance-

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext:
It is nearly double.
r 1052-32 J

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: Yes, but a large item was due to a change in policy with regard to overtime. In this department there had grown up over the years the practice of paying a large number of customs officers very large sums for overtime services. The rate paid for overtime work was substantially higher than that paid for ordinary work. During the past year we have made a substantial- I was almost going to say a drastic-change of policy in that regard, and whereas the overtime paid by the department for the year 1936-37 was $228,639.51, the overtime paid by the department for the first nine months of the present year 1937-38 was only $13,216.27. So we have cut out the greater part of our payments for overtime. But we have been obliged to take on about 140 or 145 additional officers, who appear in the item to which the hon. gentleman has referred- temporary assistance. That would be the main reason for the increase in temporaries. But there has been some increase in temporaries apart from overtime, due to the increase in activities on the frontier. There has been a tremendous increase in tourist business and also a very large increase in imports.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext:
I thank the minister
for connecting those two items, because the next question I proposed to address to him was as to the difference between the items of overtime in 1937-38 and in 1938-39. On the same page, in 1937-38 the overtime was $294,952, and for the current year it is $150,000. a difference of about $144,000 of a saving in overtime. But for temporary assistance the increase is much greater than the saving in the payments in respect of overtime.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: Not very much.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: Well, substantially so. It is an increase, and I suppose the only answer that the minister can make is that it is giving an additional number of men employment; but it is really not effecting an economy in the end.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext:
It did effect an economy. I am not sure whether it was a large economy, but it is not as my hon. friend has just put it. The number that have been taken on- are doing more work than was being done by the overtime men. There has been an increase in the number of temporaries to do the work that was performed by the officers who had been doing overtime, and there has also been an increase in the number of other temporaries. We had to do this in order to meet increased business. If we had left the overtime system as it was we would have had to increase
Supply-National Revenue

the staff substantially to take care of the increased business in export, import, tourist business and excise.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: With respect to this item No. 204, would the minister be good enough to indicate whether the appointment of the temporary employees as permanent was in the customs or the excise division or in both; and in either event what type of employee:, were they whose status was changed from temporary to permanent?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: The change of status took place in the customs and excise divisions. This vote deals with general administration at head office of the customs and excise divisions, and the change took place in both. These temporaries were made permanent.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: That is something in the routine of events; it is not a matter of taking a group?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: No.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: Following through to page 141 I find that there have been apparently several new appointments of importance. The minister will see an item with regard to a "dominion customs appraiser, values," and immediately under that there is provision for a secretary, customs division. Apparently there was not a secretary in 1937-38. Will the minister tell me the name of the present secretary and when he was appointed? Was it a civil service appointment?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: This is merely a reclassification; these individuals do not represent additional appointees. Mr. Taylor is now secretary of the customs division; last year he was head clerk. The same applies to the position of assistant secretary.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: Customs division?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext:
A little further down the
page there is provision for a chief, customs check branch. Is that a promotion or a new appointment?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: That is a promotion. My hon. friend will see that there is a large reduction in the other column of head clerks. These are simply called by different names. They are reclassifications, and do not represent new people brought in.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: May I take it that all the instances in the column showing the number of persons holding positions in 1937-38, which indicate what would appear to be new appointments in the column for 1938-39, are promotions and not new appointments?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: That is correct, yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext: But there are twenty-two new appointments.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF NATIONAL REVENUE
speechtext:
These are temporaries made permanent. If the committee would permit me, my colleague the Minister of Transport (Mr. Howe) would like to get into committee to-night, and I shall not ask that this item be passed. We could let the item stand and call an item to enable the Minister of Transport to get in.
Item stands.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT

speechtext: Marine Sendee-maintenance and repairs to wharves, $7,500.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: This is a small item for the maintenance and repair of wharves in Canada. Where are these repairs being carried out?

speakeroldname: Hon. C. D. HOWE (Minister of Transport):
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: There are some two thousand wharves entrusted to the Department of Transport for management. The item covers small repairs to these wharves, the average item being under $50. If there are major repairs to be carried out, the work is done by the Department of Public Works.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: Are these wharves in inland waters or on the sea?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: Both. Last year the following amounts were spent: Nova Scotia, $693.42; Prince Edward Island, $1,524; New Brunswick, $193; Quebec, $1,035; Montreal, $521; Prescott, $100; Parry Sound, $1,257; British Columbia, $567. These are the amounts that were spent in the different agencies.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: What is the reason for the increase in connection with lighting?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: There is no increase in the main item; it is the same as it has been for the last three years.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: An increase is shown here.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: Does $4,500 provide for the lighting of all government wharves in Canada?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: No.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: An increase is shown for lighting of $750 as compared with last year's item.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext:
There has been a reallocation of the item; the total of the item is not changed. We transferred about $1,000 out of materials and supplies into the lighting item because experience has shown that a larger expenditure is required for lighting and a lower expenditure for materials.

Supply-Transport-M arine

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: How much was spent last year out of the corresponding vote?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: Last year we spent 87,135.

Item agreed to.
To provide for breaking ice in Thunder bay, lake Superior, and other points deemed advisable in the interests of navigation, $30,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: What does "and other points" mean?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: The contract for ice-breaking in Thunder bay covers one or two small adjacent harbours. I think this is the third or fourth year this contract has been in force.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext:
What was spent last
year out of the corresponding item, and to whom were the payments made?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext:
Is it one company or
several?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: Last year there was spent 830,000. It is a contract calling for an annual payment of $30,000. The contract was with Sinmac Lines Limited.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: What does the contract require the contractor to do?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: It calls for him to open the harbour, commencing at a date set by the marine branch, and to maintain navigation in the autumn up to a date specified by the marine branch for closing navigation in that harbour. It also includes transportation of lighthouse keepers to certain lights, and opening of harbours such as Rossport and, I think, possibly one or two other small harbours nearby.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: Were tenders invited for this service, and is there a written contract for it?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: There is a written contract for it. The contract was renewed last year at the same rate as before. It is a three year contract, that expired last year and was renewed at the same rate for three more years. The price we have now is one of the lowest contract prices we have ever had for that service.

Item agreed to.
To provide for Canada's share of the cost of the north Atlantic ice patrol, $6,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: What is undertaken by Canada under this patrol?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: And with whom?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext:
The north Atlantic ice patrol was set up in 1914. Thirteen different nations are parties to the agreement. The
patrol has been managed by the United States, and the cost is divided among the various nations in agreed proportions. Canada's share of the cost is three per cent per annum, and the cost varies slightly from year to year but Canada's share never exceeding $6,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: Do Canadian ships carry out the patrol?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: The work is done by United States ships.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: What was expended last year under the corresponding vote?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: In 1936 the amount expended was $4,566, and in the previous year, $5,331.

Item agreed to.
Marine service administration, $18,040.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: Will the minister explain the increase over the previous year?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: The increase is made up of statutory increases, $240, and restoration of salary deduction, $740.25.

Item agreed to.
Administration of floating equipment, $28,835.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: What is meant by floating equipment?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: The equipment of the department, boats of all kinds, was administered in earlier years by several branches of the department, by the ship channel branch, the dominion steamers and the ice-breakers. All our boats are now administered by this branch. The moneys covered by this item were formerly in the ship channel vote, the vote for miscellaneous services relating to navigation, and the dominion steamers and ice-breakers vote. Now we have a branch which manages boats of all kinds belonging to the Department of Transport.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: I assume from the minister's statement that this vote does not include any floating equipment under the control and operation of the Department of Public Works. Those remain as they were?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: Quite right. It relates only to those of the Department of Transport.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: I understood the minister to say it included all the floating equipment of the government.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: No; the floating equipment of the Department of Transport.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: Does this include the operation of dredges?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext:
Such dredges as we have.
The Union Jack

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: While you have sold during the year, have you not, a large number of these, you still have the same number of men and the same expenditure?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: The men were there before but their duties have been reallocated. There has been a readjustment. We had no vote last year to correspond with this, but the men were in the department last year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext: Would the minister give the committee more details of the floating equipment, of what it consists?

speakerposition: Deputy Chair of Committees of the Whole
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORT
speechtext:
The minister could have that information for the next sitting.
Item stands.
Progress reported.
